Democrats flipped 41 House seats driven by suburban college-educated women voters. The economy was strong but anti-Trump sentiment dominated. Republicans held and expanded Senate majority in a very favourable map — only 9 R seats vs 26 D seats up for election.

Expected red wave failed to materialise. Dobbs decision overturning Roe v. Wade energised Democratic turnout especially among women and young voters. Republicans eked out a 9-seat House majority but significantly underperformed polling. Democrats gained a Senate seat in Pennsylvania.
